entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
William III, of the House of Massa, was the last Judge of Cagliari, ruling under the name Salusio VI from 1256 to his deposition in 1258. He is also known as Guglielmo Cepolla or Cipolla.

As the ruler of Cagliari, William III oversaw the city's decline into a minor power during the late 13th century. His reign was marked by a series of conflicts with neighboring city-states, including the Republic of Pisa and the Republic of Genoa.

William III's legacy is that of a failed statesman who could not stem the tide of decline that had begun to affect Cagliari in the mid-13th century. His deposition in 1258 marked the end of an era, and the city was eventually absorbed into the Republic of Sardinia.

The legacy of William III can also be seen in the city's architecture, which reflects the influence of the Massa family's rule during this period. The city's historic center, with its narrow streets and Gothic-style churches, is a testament to the enduring presence of the House of Massa in Cagliari's history.

The impact of William III's reign can also be seen in the historical records of the time, which provide valuable insights into the politics and society of the region during the late 13th century.

William III's story is also one of personal tragedy, as he was forced to abdicate in 1258 due to a combination of internal and external pressures.

In the centuries that followed, the legacy of William III was largely forgotten, but in recent years, there has been a growing interest in the history of the House of Massa and the city of Cagliari during this period.
